blocks.orig: From pristine beaches to breathtaking mountain ranges, Tanzania fascinates visitors from all over the world. The diverse Tanzanian nature never stops impressing with its diverse flora and fauna, unspoilt and unique to the region.
blocks.html: Tanzania captivates travellers from every corner of the globe, from its untouched beaches to its spectacular mountain ranges. The country’s varied landscapes keep on impressing with flora and fauna that are rich, unspoilt and found nowhere else.

blocks.orig: Another highlight of these natural gems is a collection of waterfalls this East African country has to offer. Here, you can leave the hustle and bustle of the Tanzanian hotspots behind and simply listen to the pure force of nature… and of course take a very refreshing shower.
blocks.html: One more highlight among these natural treasures is the collection of waterfalls that this East African country offers. Here you can escape the bustle of Tanzania’s busy hotspots and simply listen to the raw power of nature… and, naturally, enjoy a very refreshing shower.

blocks.orig: If you’ve already imagined yourself standing under the cascading waterfalls, let’s dive deeper and explore the best waterfall locations in Tanzania. But we must warn you: the following pictures might make you want to pack your suitcase still today…
blocks.html: If you can already picture yourself beneath the tumbling water, let’s go a little further and look at the finest waterfall spots in Tanzania. One warning first: the pictures below may well tempt you to pack your suitcase this very day…

blocks.orig: To get to Sanje waterfalls, you first need to conquer a somewhat challenging 4-hour hike through the jungle in the Udzungwa Mountains National Park. Yes, the trail is steep, but as soon as you reach the waterfalls, you’ll know they were worth the sore legs. As you pass through the dense forest, remember to look down and up. Why? On the trail you might encounter some elephant tracks and in the trees you could spot the rare black and white colobus monkey swinging from tree to tree. When you reach the checkpoint, you can either hike to the top of this Tanzanian waterfall or descend to the bottom of it, where you can jump into the (cold) water.
blocks.html: Reaching the Sanje waterfalls first means completing a fairly demanding 4-hour hike through the jungle of the Udzungwa Mountains National Park. The path is steep, that much is true, but once the waterfalls come into view you’ll agree they were worth the aching legs. While you walk through the thick forest, keep an eye on the ground as well as the canopy. The reason? You may come across elephant tracks on the trail, and up in the branches you could see the rare black and white colobus monkey swinging from one tree to the next. At the checkpoint you can choose between hiking to the top of this Tanzanian waterfall or climbing down to its base, where a plunge into the (cold) water awaits.

blocks.orig: Kalambo Falls is the second tallest free-leaping waterfall in Africa. The water cascades at a height of 235 metres (772 feet) and flows into Lake Tanganyika. Getting to the spot for the perfect view takes about three hours on a steep trail. As you continue climbing the canyon, you can catch a glimpse of local villagers tending to their chores and immerse yourself in the diverse nature of the region. Despite the long hike, reaching the cliff from where you can admire the Kalambo Falls is worth every drop of sweat. Another cool plus: you would be standing on the border of Tanzania and Zambia.
blocks.html: Among free-leaping waterfalls in Africa, Kalambo Falls is the second tallest. The water plunges 235 metres (772 feet) before running into Lake Tanganyika. Reaching the spot with the perfect view means roughly three hours on a steep trail. As you climb further up the canyon, you may catch sight of villagers going about their daily chores while you soak up the varied nature of the region. Long as the hike is, arriving at the cliff from which you can gaze at the Kalambo Falls repays every drop of sweat. A further bonus: you’ll be standing right on the border between Tanzania and Zambia.

blocks.orig: The Kisasa Waterfall is a majestic natural wonder located in the Usambara Mountains and is waiting to be discovered. Lush greenery and refreshing crystal-clear water are guaranteed on the spot. Once you make your way through the rainforest, you can relax and simply admire powerful waterfalls cascading down the rocks. Have a well-deserved and yummy picnic and jump into the refreshing water, before heading back with new memories and a big smile.
blocks.html: Tucked away in the Usambara Mountains, the Kisasa Waterfall is a majestic natural wonder that is still waiting to be discovered. Lush vegetation and refreshing, crystal-clear water are a certainty here. After making your way through the rainforest, you can sit back and simply watch the powerful falls tumbling over the rocks. Enjoy a tasty, well-earned picnic and jump into the cool water before you head back with fresh memories and a wide smile.

blocks.orig: The name says it all. Just that in this case, it doesn’t. The oasis of “hot springs” between Moshi and Arusha, is, in fact, filled with refreshing water. So, before you embark on the journey through the jungle to discover this place, make sure to grab your bathing suit and take a dip in the crystal-clear water. You can relax there and may even feel the slight warmth coming from the groundwater fed by Mount Kilimanjaro. The cherry on the cake are the Blue Monkeys you might spot in the surrounding fig trees.
blocks.html: Normally the name tells you everything. In this case, it doesn’t. The oasis of “hot springs” that lies between Moshi and Arusha is actually filled with refreshing water. So before you set off through the jungle to find this place, be sure to pack your swimming costume and take a dip in the crystal-clear water. It is a place to unwind, and you might even notice the gentle warmth of the groundwater that is fed by Mount Kilimanjaro. The icing on the cake are the Blue Monkeys you may spot in the surrounding fig trees.

blocks.orig: If you have a few days left in Moshi, you can also visit the Materuni Waterfall. The overall difficulty of the trail is low to average. Most of the trek is flat, only a short distance is inclined, and usually visitors reach the waterfall within an hour. Apart from admiring the magnificent Materuni Waterfall, you’ll also have a chance to speak to the locals, learning more about their culture. Unlike other locations, you can support local businesses by purchasing coffee and lunch on the way.
blocks.html: With a few days to spare in Moshi, you could also head to the Materuni Waterfall. The trail is of low to average difficulty overall. Most of the walk is flat, with only a short uphill stretch, and visitors typically reach the waterfall within an hour. Besides admiring the magnificent Materuni Waterfall, you’ll also get to talk with the local people and learn more about their culture. Unlike at other spots, you can support local businesses here by buying coffee and lunch along the way.

blocks.orig: The Ngare Sero Waterfall can be found in the Lake Natron area, nearby a Maasai village. The trail leading to the waterfall is manageable and shouldn’t take more than 30 minutes. In other words: it’s a must-see for many visitors exploring the region. On your way to this Tanzanian waterfall, prepare to get wet, since you’ll have to make your way through a hip-high river (hint: protective gear for your gadgets is key). But don’t worry, since it’s quite hot, you’ll be dry again in no time. Once you reach this magical destination, take as much time as you want to walk and swim under the Ngare Sero Fall’s cascading water.
blocks.html: You’ll find the Ngare Sero Waterfall in the Lake Natron area, close to a Maasai village. The walk to the falls is easy enough and shouldn’t take longer than 30 minutes. Put simply, it’s a must-see for many travellers exploring this region. Be prepared to get wet on the way to this Tanzanian waterfall, as you’ll need to wade through a river that comes up to your hips (tip: protection for your gadgets is essential). No need to worry, though: in this heat you’ll dry off again in no time. Once you arrive at this magical spot, take all the time you like to wander and swim beneath the cascading water of the Ngare Sero Fall.

blocks.orig: Marangu Waterfalls are also known as Ndoro and Monjo, which literally translates into ‘nature’ and ‘water always’. Hiking to that beauty spot is fairly easy, even if you travel during rainy season. However, you should equip yourself with non-slippery shoes just to be on the safe side. If you want to end your Kilimanjaro climbing adventure with a smaller but also wow highlight, the Marangu Waterfall is the palace to be. You’ll notice how the local community is thriving here, and you’ll get the chance to taste local coffee. What’s not to love?
blocks.html: The Marangu Waterfalls go by the names Ndoro and Monjo as well, which literally mean ‘nature’ and ‘water always’. The hike to this beauty spot is quite easy, even in the rainy season. Still, to be on the safe side, bring non-slippery shoes. If you’d like to round off your Kilimanjaro climbing adventure with a smaller yet still impressive highlight, the Marangu Waterfall is the place to go. You’ll see how well the local community is doing here, and you’ll have the chance to try the local coffee. What’s not to love?
